quotations.text: The patient-physician relationship is a moral activity that arises from the obligation of the physician to alleviate suffering and respect the patient’s beliefs and autonomy.
quotations.work: WMA Declaration of Cordoba on Patient-Physician Relationship
quotations.context_note: The declaration describes the patient-physician relationship as a moral relationship grounded in care, beliefs, autonomy, trust, and shared decision making.
quotations.use_note: Use to illuminate the moral character of professional relationship; not to adjudicate any disputed clinical encounter.

quotations.text: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.
quotations.context_note: Article 1 states a universal human-rights premise about dignity and equality.
quotations.use_note: Use as a human-rights reference for dignity and equality; not as a substitute for jurisdiction-specific law.

quotations.text: full and equal access to their health care services and facilities
quotations.work: Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities
quotations.context_note: DOJ guidance explains ADA and, where applicable, Section 504 accessibility duties for medical settings, including reasonable modifications.
quotations.use_note: U.S.-jurisdiction legal guidance only; educational context, not individualized legal advice.

quotations.text: You deserve to feel heard and cared about anytime, anywhere, 24/7/365.
quotations.context_note: The Lifeline describes support as available for emotional distress and other difficult moments; a person does not have to be suicidal to contact 988.
quotations.use_note: Use to describe a U.S. support option, not as evidence that crisis intervention is appropriate for every person who is suffering.

crisis.confidentiality: officially described by 988 as confidential; confidential is not the same as anonymous

quotations.text: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;
quotations.context_note: The verse appears within a larger passage describing love. The quotation is used here specifically for the relation between love and truth.
quotations.use_note: Spiritual correspondence only; never evidence for a disputed historical or professional claim.

quotations.context_note: The JPS 1985 verse also prohibits vengeance and bearing a grudge against one’s countrymen. Jewish interpretation is not collapsed into Christian uses of the same textual source.
quotations.use_note: Spiritual correspondence only; not a claim of doctrinal equivalence or factual proof.

quotations.text: whoever saves a life, it will be as if they saved all of humanity.
quotations.translation_or_version: The Clear Quran, Dr. Mustafa Khattab, as displayed by Quran.com
quotations.context_note: The quoted phrase is part of a verse framed as an ordinance for the Children of Israel and must not be detached from that context.
quotations.use_note: Spiritual correspondence about preservation of life; not a universal clinical directive for a particular person.

quotations.text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased.
quotations.authority_level: Buddhist canonical teaching in cited translation
quotations.context_note: Verse 5 appears among teachings on hatred, retaliation, and the mental conditions that sustain conflict.
quotations.use_note: Use to illuminate restraint and non-retaliation; not to erase accountability or factual disagreement.

quotations.text: I WILL RESPECT the autonomy and dignity of my patient;
quotations.context_note: The current pledge pairs patient autonomy and dignity within a broader professional commitment to health, human life, confidentiality, conscience, and human rights.
quotations.use_note: Professional ethical context; not a finding about any individual physician.

quotations.text: the right to the enjoyment of the highest attainable standard of health without discrimination on the basis of disability
quotations.work: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
quotations.context_note: Article 25 addresses health access, non-discrimination, informed consent, professional training, and equal quality of care for persons with disabilities.
quotations.use_note: International human-rights context; implementation and enforceability depend on jurisdiction.

quotations.text: To courtesy, respect, dignity, and timely, responsive attention to their needs.
quotations.work: AMA Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 1.1.3 — Patient Rights
quotations.context_note: The opinion presents patient rights within a mutually respectful patient-physician alliance and also addresses information, decision making, privacy, records, second opinions, and continuity.
quotations.use_note: Professional ethical guidance; not legal advice and not an adjudication of alleged misconduct.

quotations.text: The enjoyment of the highest attainable standard of health is one of the fundamental rights of every human being
quotations.work: Constitution of the World Health Organization
quotations.context_note: The WHO Constitution places this principle among foundational commitments concerning health, international cooperation, public participation, and governmental responsibility.
quotations.use_note: Global-health and human-rights context; not a guarantee of a particular treatment or individualized legal entitlement.
